title: Attention by hand in NumPy, with a heatmap
setup:
import numpy as _np
Q = _np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0], [0.5, -0.5]])
K = _np.array([[1.0, 0.5], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, -1.0], [0.5, 0.5]])
V = _np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 2.0], [3.0, 1.0], [0.5, 0.5]])
def _ref_attention(Q, K, V, causal=False):
    s = Q @ K.T / _np.sqrt(K.shape[1])
    if causal:
        s = _np.where(_np.triu(_np.ones(s.shape, dtype=bool), 1), -_np.inf, s)
    w = _np.exp(s - s.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))
    w = w / w.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return w @ V, w
checks: The output matches scaled dot-product attention
_np.allclose(attention(Q, K, V, causal=True)[1], _ref_attention(Q, K, V, True)[1])
Each row of weights sums to 1
Token 1 cannot attend to token 2 under the mask
Large scores do not overflow (no NaN)
